context: Continuation of specs/parser-check-cp2 (CP2a, complete 31/31). This feature covers the two never-planned parts of CP2: CP2a-bridge (FR-011, this repo's dependency floor and bundled index) and CP2b (US2/US3/US4, FR-012..FR-040 -- flextools_try_word, flextools_parse_status, the morph resolver and the run machinery). intent: Plan the remaining half of parser-check CP2, chosen by the user over three other readings of '/speckit-plan CP2-SPEC.md'.

decisions.decision: Plan CP2b + CP2a-bridge in a new feature directory, leaving the completed CP2a artifacts untouched.

Bridge lands as one unit (floor + index + equality test). The equality test compares the version server/versioning.py resolves (live-module-first), NOT importlib.metadata, which reads 4.8.0 here against a 4.9.0 tree. Proving the published distribution installs is a separate task with its own evidence line.

CP2b introduces a long-lived parse worker process, one per project, holding the LCM cache and the grammar. Forced by R-02: this server process never opens a project, and a one-shot subprocess cannot satisfy FR-031/FR-042/SC-009/SC-014.

check_active_parser runs as the first statement of the WORKER's request handler, not the server handler, because it reads an open project. FR-015's substance ('before any parser is constructed') is satisfied strictly and guarded by a zero-parser-calls test.

The bridge regenerates three flexicon-version-locked artifacts, not the two the Verbatim Constraints name; common_patterns_flexicon-v<ver>.json sits one directory up. Equality asserts over a discovered set, never a hardcoded pair.
tests/test_cp1_boundary.py is amended (scope narrowed in writing, worker allowlist pinned by a test), never deleted or weakened.
The three CP2a read-gap accessors get tests in flexicon BEFORE the resolver is written -- CP2a's debt by origin, CP2b's precondition by dependency.
The floor/index equality test discovers artifacts by pattern over BOTH _v and -v separators and asserts a vacuity guard, rather than checking a hardcoded pair.
decisions.why: D-B4 was right and understated: there are three flexicon-locked artifacts, and common_patterns_flexicon-v4.9.0.json uses a - separator while the other two use _. A hardcoded pair would have ignored the third permanently; a discovery sweep with a broken pattern would pass vacuously over an empty set.
decisions.rejected: Hardcoding the two artifacts the Verbatim Constraints name.

decisions.decision: Dropped the source-introspection shape guards from the flexicon GetGenres test instead of making them work.
decisions.why: Both claims were already covered behaviorally, and GetGenres is decorated with @wrap_enumerable which does not use functools.wraps -- so getsource() returned the decorator body and inspect.unwrap() could not follow it. A guard that goes red for a reason it is not about is a guard that gets deleted.
decisions.rejected: Closure-walking machinery to recover the undecorated source.

decisions.decision: server/parse/__init__.py exports nothing and imports none of its own submodules.
decisions.why: The package spans two processes. A convenience re-export would be a server-process import of worker_main by the back door, defeating R-02 and the one-worker-per-project ownership the package exists to express.
decisions.rejected: A conventional facade __init__ re-exporting the public names.

decisions.decision: ensure_grammar asks IsUpToDate() but never calls Reload() on a parse path
decisions.why: the facade already confirms currency and reloads on every parse; calling Reload() would be a second currency path (the sibling of the one spec.md Delta 2 forbids) and would discard a grammar the facade was about to load, paying the most expensive step twice
decisions.rejected: calling Reload() on first use, which ground-truth showed produces a byte-identical trace

decisions.decision: worker channel is ASCII-only on the wire plus UTF-8 stdio in the child
decisions.why: Windows stdio defaulted to cp1252 and silently replaced non-ASCII; IndonesianHC-Complete is written in IPA so this corrupted every word
decisions.rejected: relying on the default console encoding

decisions.decision: T059/T060 done early, out of Phase 6 order
decisions.why: the CP1 boundary test went red the moment T026 landed (exactly as research.md R-06 predicted); leaving the suite red through Phases 3-5 would mask new failures

BLOCKS T021/T022 AS WRITTEN: subprocess_helpers.run_script_async is one-shot -- it calls process.communicate() (waits for exit) with stdin=DEVNULL, so it cannot host a long-lived worker speaking line-delimited JSON on stdin/stdout. T022 says to launch through the existing run_script_async FAMILY and to tear down via _kill_process_tree. Reading that as a sibling launcher in the same module, sharing _kill_process_tree and the start_new_session process-group discipline, is the only way to satisfy both halves; calling run_script_async literally is impossible. Needs confirmation before the worker is built.

flexicon HeadlessLcmUI.SynchronizeInvoke returns None and liblcm dereferences it unguarded in SendPropChangedNotifications; a loaded HC parser is the change-watcher its issue-285 contingency warned about, so any headless WRITE while a grammar is held crashes. FlexToolsMCP is unaffected (worker opens read-only) but this should be filed upstream on flexicon.

FR-018.title: The restricted trace MUST accept a decomposition expressed in terms a caller can actually write -- entry headwords, headword plus sense, or internal identifiers -- and resolve it t

FR-019.title: If any piece of a decomposition resolves to no usable analysis, the request MUST be refused, naming the piece, its position and its candidates, and no parse MUST be run.

FR-020.title: Lookup structures used for resolution MUST be built once per run and reused across words.

FR-021.title: Where every piece has exactly one unambiguous candidate, the system MAY offer a proposed decomposition; when it does, it MUST label it proposed and unverified.

FR-022.title: Guidance offered when a decomposition is missing MUST name only actions the caller can actually perform with the tools that exist.

FR-023.title: A caller's proposed decomposition MUST always be traced exactly as given. The system MUST NOT substitute a different restriction, widen it to an unrestricted search, reorder, score

FR-025.title: Agreement between a proposal and recorded analyses MUST produce no commentary.

FR-026.title: All parser execution MUST go through one run mechanism. There MUST NOT be a separate synchronous path.

FR-027.title: A run MUST report a distinct stage for starting, loading the grammar, parsing, filing (defined but unreachable in this checkpoint), completed, failed and cancelled.

FR-028.title: A run reaching a terminal stage inside a configurable grace window (default 5 seconds) MUST return its results inline; otherwise it MUST return a handle. The window governs reporti

FR-030.title: Runs MUST be ordered by the same priority levels and ordering the host application uses, lowest value first, first-in-first-out within a level, enqueued per word.

FR-031.title: A higher-priority single word MUST interleave at the running batch's next word boundary. The batch MUST NOT restart or lose position, the grammar MUST NOT be reloaded, and the batc

FR-032.title: Cancellation MUST be cooperative, stopping at the next word boundary and leaving a cancelled terminal stage over the partial results.

FR-033.title: The assistant MUST offer a read-only status tool taking a run handle and reporting stage, progress, and -- on a terminal stage -- the result summary or the failure with its guidanc

FR-034.title: A failed run MUST carry guidance pointing at the diagnostic instruments, since memory exhaustion is the case where a diagnosis beats a retry.

FR-035.title: A status request for an unknown handle MUST be refused naming the handle and the handles that do exist.

FR-036.title: A cancelled run MUST be reportable with the count of words completed and the stage it was in when cancelled. Reporting a cancelled run's status is not itself a refusal; the cancell
